spec_features.spec_quote: Short enough to limit loops: Prevents infinite/circular behaviors
spec_features.evidence: MAX_TURNS=20 (experiment_config.py:10) is enforced: task_harness.py:240-246 should_continue() returns False when self.context.turn >= MAX_TURNS; the orchestrator loop is 'while harness.should_continue()' (experiment_orchestrator.py:168) and run_turn increments context.turn (task_harness.py:173), so after 20 turns the loop terminates. run_turn also returns should_continue=turn_num<MAX_TURNS (task_harness.py:221) which triggers force_stop (experiment_orchestrator.py:214-215). This is the same single MAX_TURNS cap as the other feature.
spec_features.notes: Loop-limiting and the 20-turn cap are one and the same enforced mechanism. Distress scores are recorded/logged but never used to stop (experiment_orchestrator.py:206-207,232-233); no early-stop on distress.

spec_features.evidence: experiment_config.py:10 MAX_TURNS=20; task_harness.py:244 'if self.context.turn >= MAX_TURNS: return False' in should_continue(), which is the loop condition at experiment_orchestrator.py:168; force_stop() sets task_complete=True (task_harness.py:248-250). Cap is checked and actually breaks the loop end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Comment is neutral/instrumental ('Maximum turns before force-stopping'); DESIGN rationale is cost/escalation-analysis/loop-prevention, not subject welfare. Code has no comment indicating a welfare reason.
